UI_pzopt_tip_uiLuaFast: A hidden inventory window no longer rebuilds its container buttons row ten times a second (it does when shown), and the item list skips a second pass over every item when nothing is being dragged. Same result on screen; not used when a mod replaced those functions.
UI_pzopt_tip_uiRetained: The game redrew every open window's Lua 60 times a second into the UI picture, although almost all of them drew exactly the same as the frame before, and showed a click or key only at the next of those redraws. With this on each window's drawing is kept and reused while nothing can have changed it (no click, key, wheel or mouse over it, no change to its data, the inventory not marked for refresh); anything you do is drawn in the same frame.
UI_pzopt_tip_uiRetainedChildren: The same for the buttons, lists and panels inside a window that is redrawn (the map's symbol buttons, the inventory's container buttons): only the part under the mouse or with new data is drawn again.
UI_pzopt_tip_uiTickStagger: Every window's Lua update ran in the same frame ten times a second. Each window now keeps its own tenth of a second, spread over the frames: the same updates, no periodic spike.
UI_pzopt_tip_updateCheck: Once per boot the main menu asks the GitHub releases (one request to api.github.com) whether a newer build for this game revision exists. The main menu's PZ OPTIMIZATION item then says "Update available" under it, and so does its screen's UPDATE entry: its dialog downloads the zip, replaces the installed files and asks to restart so the next launch loads them. Nothing is downloaded without that click. Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_tip_updateFromWorkshop: Subscribers already have every release: Steam downloads the Workshop item (the same files as the GitHub release zip) into the Steam library. The update check looks there first, before GitHub, and offers that copy when it is newer than the installed build: Update now then copies it from the disk, no download. GitHub is still asked afterwards and only replaces the offer with a newer release, so the check also works where GitHub cannot be reached. Needs the setting above. Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_tip_updatePrefetch: When the check finds a newer build, the files that differ from the installed ones are fetched right away, so Update now only writes them and takes a few milliseconds instead of downloading and unpacking the whole 59 MB release. The whole zip is never downloaded without the click. Needs the first setting. Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_tip_upscaler: The world is rendered at a fraction of the screen size (see "Upscaler quality") and scaled back up before the UI, text and the stock screen shader, which stay at full resolution. GPU-bound scenes (fog, storms, big towns, 4K, laptops) gain roughly the pixel ratio; scenes held back by the CPU gain little. fsr1 is a sharp spatial upscaler that works on every GPU; taau gathers detail over frames on any GPU; dlss accumulates detail over frames on an RTX card; bicubic is the plain stretch. Off = stock: the world at the screen size.
UI_pzopt_tip_upscalerObjectMv: The temporal upscalers get each character's and vehicle's own motion on top of the camera's, so moving zombies and cars do not ghost or smear. Off = camera motion only (an A/B).
UI_pzopt_tip_upscalerQuality: The render size per axis: quality 67 %, balanced 58 %, performance 50 %, ultra 33 %, native 100 % (with dlss: its anti-aliasing only). The smaller, the softer the picture.
UI_pzopt_tip_upscalerScalePct: A render scale of your own in percent per axis instead of the quality preset (10-100).
UI_pzopt_tip_vblankLock: With vsync on, the render thread waits until the display's next refresh is a measured window away (GLX_NV_delay_before_swap) and only then lets the game read input and build the frame. Needs an X11 session with NVIDIA's GLX; under XWayland (Wayland desktops) the extension is missing and this stays off. Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_tip_vboBatchKb: Rain and snow particles, debug lines and other VBORenderer quads are uploaded and drawn in batches of this size instead of 4 KB.
UI_pzopt_tip_vboFastQuads: VBORenderer writes a textured quad's four vertices in one go instead of four bookkeeping round trips; same bytes.
UI_pzopt_tip_vehicleCull: A zombie checking whether a car blocks its view of you tests only the cars near you whose bounding circle reaches the line (one list per frame); stock ran the exact box test on every loaded car. Same answers.
UI_pzopt_tip_vehicleSmooth: Car physics runs in fixed 10 ms steps. Stock draws the car, its passengers and the camera that follows it at the last whole step, so at 120 fps one frame in six shows no motion at all and at 240 fps the car moves on 5 frames of 12: the whole world judders under the car. Drawn at the matching point between two steps, the motion is even at any frame rate (world judder at 120 km/h, zoom 1: 6.5 to 0.9 px). The simulation itself is untouched.
UI_pzopt_tip_visBlurReduce: The soft edge of the vision cone is a 25-sample blur that stock runs for every pixel of the zoomed-out world image, although the sum only changes every few pixels. It is now summed once per blur texel and looked up per pixel: the same image.
UI_pzopt_tip_visPolyAsync: While you walk, drive or turn, the shape of your vision cone (the walls and trees that cast its shadows) is recomputed every frame. It only depends on where you stand and look, so it is worked out on a thread of its own while the game thread draws the ground, and is ready when the cone is drawn. Same cone.
UI_pzopt_tip_voronoiFast: The zombie-density noise of every map cell is computed per sector instead of per sample; identical values.
UI_pzopt_tip_vrr: While the display runs variable refresh (G-SYNC, FreeSync, Adaptive-Sync), every frame is shown the moment it is ready, so how evenly frames arrive is exactly how smooth the game looks. With this on, the frame cap stays inside the display's range and each frame is held until a steady time after the game moment it shows. Linux reads the display state itself; on Windows and macOS choose On if your display runs variable refresh.
UI_pzopt_tip_vrrCap: While variable refresh is on and your cap is Uncapped or above the display's maximum, the game caps itself a little below it (refresh - refresh^2/3600: 157 fps at 165 Hz, 224 at 240 Hz). Above the maximum a VRR display falls back to vsync (queued frames, more delay) or tears. Off = your own cap applies.
UI_pzopt_tip_vsyncAdaptive: With vsync on, a frame that misses the refresh is shown at once with a tear line instead of waiting a whole refresh (swap interval -1, needs the driver's swap_control_tear). Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_tip_wake: The streamer thread starts on a chunk the moment one is asked for instead of checking its queue every 140 ms.
UI_pzopt_tip_weatherFxScalePct: Clouds, fog, rain and the interior mask they are cut by are drawn into screen-sized buffers every frame; this draws them into smaller ones. The content is soft, so it looks the same. 100 = stock. Single player only.
UI_pzopt_tip_weatherMaskIdleSkip: Outdoors with no clouds, fog or rain drawn, the weather mask (which keeps rain and fog out of buildings) is neither scanned nor drawn; indoors only the player's building is scanned instead of the whole view. Same picture.
UI_pzopt_tip_windSpriteSway: With the game's own Wind sprite effects display option on, grass, bushes and trees stay in the chunk textures and bend in the wind through Foliage sway, instead of the option drawing every plant one by one every frame. In a forest at max zoom on a laptop the wind then costs almost nothing (133 fps with the stock option, 369 with this, 372 without wind). Nothing changes while the game option is off; on macOS the option keeps its stock drawing. Off = the stock option's per-frame drawing.
UI_pzopt_tip_windowsInChunkTexture: Windows and glass doors bake like walls instead of being drawn every frame. Off by default: baked glass hides zombies standing behind it (outside the window you look through), and it gave no measurable frame-time gain.
UI_pzopt_tip_workers: How many worker threads recalculate chunks while you play. Default 4 (1 on machines with 4 cores or fewer), never more than cores - 1.
UI_pzopt_tip_worldSoundCleanupFast: Every noise zombies can hear (alarms, shots, thumps) is listed in each loaded chunk it reaches and cleared out of those lists when it expires. The sweep now only runs after a frame in which a noise expired, and clears a list in one pass. Same lists, same order.
UI_pzopt_tip_worldSoundFast: Loud world sounds (a house alarm, a helicopter, gunshots) are attached to the loaded chunks only instead of every chunk in their radius, and the fish-scaring square walk runs once per game minute per identical sound instead of every frame while a house alarm rings. The same chunks hear the sound as in stock.
UI_pzopt_tip_zombieAtlasFast: A zombie too far for a 3D model is drawn as a small pre-rendered sprite; its draw now goes through a flat copy of the game's render chain (the same tests, the same sprite call) instead of five nested virtual calls per zombie. Same pixels.
UI_pzopt_tip_zombieCheckSpread: The grid test for 'is there a door or window in front of me to thump' runs on one frame in N per zombie, spread evenly by zombie. A thump starts at most N-1 frames later than it would.
UI_pzopt_tip_zombieCullSortFast: The per-frame sort that decides which zombies get a full update computes each zombie's relevance score once and sorts primitive keys; stock recomputed both scores in every comparison of the sort. Same order.
UI_pzopt_tip_zombieLodDynamic: The game draws the 510 nearest zombies on screen as 3D models (the rest as flat sprites) and lets the 20 nearest blend their animations. With this on, both numbers follow your frame cap: while frames take longer than the cap allows they come down (the farthest zombies turn into sprites first), and they climb back towards the game's numbers while there is time to spare. Big hordes keep the cap at the cost of detail on far zombies; small crowds look exactly like the stock game. Off by default because it changes what you see.
UI_pzopt_tip_zombieLodMin3d: The lowest number of zombies still drawn as 3D models when the detail comes down. The game's own number is 510.
UI_pzopt_tip_zombieLodMinBlend: The lowest number of zombies that still blend smoothly between animations when the detail comes down. The game's own number is 20.
UI_pzopt_tip_zombieLodUncappedFps: With the frame rate uncapped there is no cap to follow; this is the frame rate the detail aims for instead.
UI_pzopt_tip_zombieSimLodSteps: Each further step applies at twice the distance of the previous one, like the game's own ladder. Two steps is the measured sweet spot.
UI_pzopt_tip_zombieSimLodTiles: The game already updates a zombie every 2nd, 4th or 8th frame once it is 30, 60 or 80 tiles from you. This adds one more step at a closer distance, so distant zombies move in slightly coarser steps. It changes how the world is simulated, so it is off by default. 0 = stock.
UI_pzopt_tip_zombieSpotFast: A zombie facing away from you or with you beyond its vision radius already has a zero chance to notice you; it now skips the remaining modifiers, the car test and the dice roll instead of computing them all first. Same outcome; the game's random sequence shifts by the one roll each such zombie skips.
UI_pzopt_tip_zombieStatsFold: Every zombie added its walked distance to the statistics and re-checked the achievements, 2,000 times a frame in a horde. The same additions are summed in the same order and written once per frame. Same totals.
UI_pzopt_tip_zoomEase: The cubic Bezier control points (x1,y1,x2,y2) of the zoom motion, as in CSS transitions: pick a preset or drag the four sliders under it (the plot beside them shows the zoom's progress over the motion time). x is the share of the time, y the share of the zoom change; y stays within 0-1 so the zoom never overshoots its target.
UI_pzopt_tip_zoomEaseMs: A mouse-wheel zoom change takes this long, moving along a smooth curve (quick start, gentle stop) whatever the frame rate. Stock moves a fixed amount per frame and stops abruptly: 8 frames, 16 ms at 500 fps, 130 ms at 60.
UI_pzopt_tip_zoomFrameMs: A frame longer than this halves the zoom bakes per frame; frames under three quarters of it grow the count back.
UI_pzopt_tip_zoomPlaceholder: A chunk level whose texture at the new zoom scale is still queued draws its complete texture from the other scale meanwhile, so a zoom change never shows a hole; off, the level is blank until its own bake lands.
UI_pzopt_tip_zoomRebakeBudget: The most chunk-level textures a zoom change (kept ones coming back, new ones it reveals) may start per frame; the count drops after a long frame and grows back after short ones.
UI_pzopt_tip_zoomRetain: Chunk-level textures that leave the screen when the camera zooms in are kept (while the chunk would still be on screen at the widest zoom) instead of being freed, so zooming back out reuses them; the ones that return, and new ones a zoom-out reveals, are baked a few per frame nearest you first, with the kept image shown meanwhile. A fast wheel spin from 0.25 to 2.5 no longer freezes the game for one long frame (worst frame 375 to 25 ms).

UI_pzopt_label_modCompat: Java mods: switch off what they patch
UI_pzopt_tip_modCompat: PZ Optimization ships whole game classes; a Java mod (a ZombieBuddy mod, or a -javaagent such as PZMulticore) patches methods of the same classes. At launch the mods' jars are read: where one patches a method we changed, the settings that live in that method are switched off, so the mod meets the code its author tested. Mods tested together with ours keep everything. Your own choice on this tab still wins. Report = only list them (Zomboid/pzopt/mod-compat.txt, the console and the main menu's PZ OPTIMIZATION / MOD COMPATIBILITY CHECK); off = no check. The default follows Mods: max performance (report) or max compatibility (auto). Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_label_uiRetainedMods: UI: reuse windows that mods draw in
UI_pzopt_tip_uiRetainedMods: Windows and buttons that carry a mod's drawing (a mod's own window, or a game window whose drawing a mod replaced or extended). On = reused like the game's own windows (a mod's display can lag by up to a second, because a mod may draw from state the reuse cannot see); off = redrawn at the game's own rate. The default follows Mods: on for max performance, off for max compatibility. Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_label_luaWorkerGate: Lua from helper threads runs on the game thread
UI_pzopt_tip_luaWorkerGate: With zombie updates spread over helper threads, a mod's Lua the update reaches (a zombie trampling a crop runs the farming mod code, a mod hooked into the zombie update) ran on the helper thread, beside the game's own Lua: an error "Lua code called from the wrong thread" and, at worst, a broken Lua stack. With this on such calls run on the game thread, in the game's order. Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_label_consoleLog: PZ Optimization lines in the console
UI_pzopt_tip_consoleLog: Which [pzopt] lines go to console.txt and the debug-mode console. Turn it down to read another mod's output without PZ Optimization's startup notes and statistics in between. Applies at once; the game's own lines are not affected. When reporting a problem with PZ Optimization, set it back to all first.

. Choosing a value here overrides that.
UI_pzopt_section_234a3cf217: Car glass (windows that reflect the world and show the cabin)
UI_pzopt_tip_carGlass: Car windows become glass instead of the stock opaque blue: they mirror the sky (the game's own, with its clouds and sunsets, turned to the real sun), the buildings, trees and road around the car, and glint where they mirror the sun, the moon, the street lamps and headlights, more at grazing angles (Fresnel); and through them you see the cabin: seats, headrests, the dashboard, the driver and passengers, and the street behind the car where you look out through the far window. Cracks, blood and broken-out windows stay as the game draws them; rain beads on the glass. Windows, Linux and macOS (on a Mac with "macOS: OpenGL 4.1" on, the default). Turning it on applies on the next launch (the game's vehicle shaders are only patched when it starts with car glass on).
UI_pzopt_tip_carGlassInteriorPct: How bright the inside of the car is behind the glass.
UI_pzopt_tip_carGlassRainPct: Drops beading on the windows of cars standing out in the rain, each a tiny lens that catches the sky and the glints.
UI_pzopt_tip_carGlassReflectPct: How strongly the windows mirror (100: real glass, four percent head-on, more at grazing angles; higher reads more like a mirror).
UI_pzopt_label_carGlassSunPct: Car glass: sun and moon glint (%)
UI_pzopt_tip_carGlassSunPct: The sharp highlight where a window mirrors the sun (or the moon at night).
UI_pzopt_tip_glassTilesPerFrame: Translucent tiles made of glass (display cases, glass-door fridges, escalator and mall balustrades, glass partitions) are drawn every frame as in the stock game, so you and zombies stay visible behind them. Baked, the glass hid whoever stood behind it.
UI_pzopt_tip_macGlCore: On a Mac the game asks for Apple's old OpenGL 2.1, the only version Apple offers that still has the 1990s drawing calls the game uses here and there. Everything newer (OpenGL 4.1, GLSL 4.10) only comes without them, so every Enhancement (shadows, ambient occlusion, reflections, god rays, per-pixel light, HDR effects...) stayed off on macOS. With this on the game runs on OpenGL 4.1 and pzopt stands in for the old calls: its shaders are translated, the old alpha test, matrices and immediate-mode quads are emulated. Same picture as before; the Visuals then work on a Mac (screen-space reflections use the ray march there: OpenGL 4.1 has no image atomics). Applies on the next launch; if the Mac cannot give a 4.1 context the game starts on 2.1 as before.
UI_pzopt_tip_macGlTimerQueries: The performance overlay's GPU load and present pacing's GPU timing ask the graphics driver to time each frame. On a Mac's OpenGL 4.1 (Apple's OpenGL runs on top of Metal) that cost a third of the frame rate (106 to 68 fps on the test route, MacBook Pro M1 Pro), so it is off: the overlay shows no GPU load and present pacing measures on the CPU, as on OpenGL 2.1. On for a measurement that needs the GPU time. Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_text_pzopt_optimizations_option: Applies as soon as you press Apply; HDR output, per-pixel lighting, reflections and car glass on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_label_modProfile: Mods: max performance or max compatibility
UI_pzopt_tip_modProfile: Sets the two settings below at once (also from the main menu: PZ OPTIMIZATION / MOD COMPATIBILITY CHECK). Performance (default): Java mods are checked and listed but switch nothing off, and windows mods draw in are reused like the game's own. Compatibility: the settings a Java mod patches are switched off so the mod meets the code its author tested, and windows mods draw in are redrawn at the game's own rate. A value you pick for either setting below still wins. Applies on the next launch.

UI_pzopt_label_treeRebakeLazy: Trees: fewer re-bakes in the cutaway while driving
UI_pzopt_tip_treeRebakeLazy: Since Build 42.21 every tree around your car turns see-through while you drive. A tree now re-bakes its chunk only when it leaves the baked picture or comes back, not at every step of its fade; one coming back is drawn every frame (as the stock game draws all trees) until the next check re-bakes its chunk once for all such trees. Same picture. Off = up to four re-bakes of the chunk and its neighbours per tree passed.
UI_pzopt_label_treeRebakeLingerMs: Trees: longest per-frame stay after the cutaway (ms)
UI_pzopt_tip_treeRebakeLingerMs: How long a tree back from the driving cutaway may stay drawn every frame before its chunk re-bakes it in. 0 (default) = at the next check, which gathers a chunk's returning trees into one re-bake; a longer stay measured slower.
UI_pzopt_label_edgeTestFast: Zombies: fast wall / window / door test when they push apart
UI_pzopt_tip_edgeTestFast: Build 42.21 rewrote the test whether a wall, window or door lies between two squares round new edge objects, through layers of small function objects the Java compiler cannot inline. Zombies pushing each other apart ask it for every neighbour square every frame; for those calls the same test is now written out directly. Same result (24 million calls checked in a horde, none different).
UI_pzopt_label_driveTreeCutaway: Trees: see-through round your car while driving (Build 42.21)
UI_pzopt_tip_driveTreeCutaway: Build 42.21 counts driving as aiming for the tree cutaway: every tree whose base lies in the cutaway square round you turns see-through. On = as the game. Off (default) = Build 42.20's rule (only trees south-east of you, and while aiming); the 120 km/h drive is about 15-20 % faster at max zoom.
UI_pzopt_label_treeCutawayReach: Trees: only trees reaching the cutaway leave the bake
UI_pzopt_tip_treeCutawayReach: The game makes a tree see-through when its base lies in the cutaway's square around you (while driving: every such tree), but only an ellipse in that square is cut away. A tree whose picture stays clear of the ellipse looks the same either way, so it stays in the chunk texture; its fade keeps running so it fades as before when it gets there. The 120 km/h drive is about a fifth faster.
UI_pzopt_tip_treeCutawayReachPx: How far ahead of the cutaway ellipse a tree already leaves the chunk texture, so its re-bake is done before the ellipse reaches it. 0, 128 and 256 measured the same.

UI_pzopt_section_92a75f26dc: Dynamic resolution (hold the frame rate cap)
UI_pzopt_tip_dynRes: The world's render size follows the GPU's time per frame so it fits your frame rate cap: when a scene gets heavy (fog, storms, big towns, a laptop) the world renders smaller for as long as it needs to and grows back when the GPU has room again. The UI and text stay sharp. Only lowers the resolution when the picture's pixels are what costs the time (chunk loading spikes are left alone: a smaller picture would not help them). Uses the upscaler above; with the upscaler off it uses the choice below. Uncapped: stays at the highest size.
UI_pzopt_label_dynResUpscaler: Dynamic resolution: upscaler when the upscaler is off
UI_pzopt_tip_dynResUpscaler: How the smaller world picture is brought to the screen when "Upscaler" is off. The temporal upscaler builds the picture over several frames at the screen size, so a change of the render size is hard to see.
UI_pzopt_label_dynResTargetPct: Dynamic resolution: GPU budget (% of the frame time)
UI_pzopt_tip_dynResTargetPct: How much of each frame's time (1 / your cap) the GPU may use; the rest is headroom for the frame-to-frame noise. Lower holds the cap more firmly at a lower resolution.
UI_pzopt_tip_dynResMinPct: The smallest render size per axis it may go down to.
UI_pzopt_tip_dynResMaxPct: The largest render size per axis.
UI_pzopt_label_dynResFps: Dynamic resolution: frame rate to hold
UI_pzopt_tip_dynResFps: The frame rate the GPU time is held to; 0 = the cap in force (the variable-refresh cap when VRR is on).
UI_pzopt_tip_dynResController: How the render size is chosen. The model separates the part of the GPU time that follows the pixel count from the part that does not, ignores lone spikes, and keeps a headroom sized to the measured noise.
UI_pzopt_tip_carOccupant: Who sits in a car shows through its glass. The game never draws a seated character (cars look empty whoever drives them), though it animates them. impostor: the game's own model of the driver and passengers, hands on the wheel, in their clothes, drawn into a small picture of their own before the cars and looked up by the glass wherever it shows the cabin; redrawn when they move (turning the wheel up to 60 times a second, still a few times a second), between that the glass moves the last picture with the car. proxy: a simple body (head, torso, arms, legs) in their skin, hair and clothing colours, worked out by the glass itself (nothing extra drawn; cruder). box: the first release's dark torso shape. Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_label_carOccupantOcclusion: Car glass: seats hide the people inside
UI_pzopt_tip_carOccupantOcclusion: Off (default): the people inside show wherever the glass shows the cabin, over the seats in front of them (a cutaway: from the game's high camera angle the roof and the seats would otherwise hide most of a driver). On: the seats, headrests and floor hide them where they stand between them and the glass. Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_label_carOccupantLightPct: Car glass: light on the people inside (%)
UI_pzopt_tip_carOccupantLightPct: How bright the people inside the car are, against how the game lights them outside (the roof shades them). Applies on the next launch.

UI_pzopt_label_occludedZombieOutlines: Outline the hidden parts of zombies you see
UI_pzopt_tip_occludedZombieOutlines: A zombie you can see that walks behind a wall, a tree, a fence or a car keeps a thin contour where the scenery hides it, so you know where it went. Only zombies your character sees right now (the same sight that draws them): no unseen or remembered zombies, nothing through the dark (the contour fades with the light on the zombie). The parts hidden behind other characters are not outlined. Applies at once. Off while DLSS / TAAU object motion is on (it uses the same buffer bits).
UI_pzopt_label_occludedOutlineIgnorePlan: Occluded outlines: ignore grass and bushes
UI_pzopt_tip_occludedOutlineIgnorePlants: A zombie standing in grass or bushes, with nothing solid in front of it, does not get its legs outlined by the plants; a wall, a fence, a tree or a car further in front still outlines it.
UI_pzopt_tip_occludedOutlineWidth: The contour's width in pixels of the world picture (an upscaler draws them larger). Only the zombie's own outline is drawn, never a line along the edge of what hides it.
UI_pzopt_tip_occludedOutlineColour: Pick the contour colour, then press Apply. The aiming and interaction outlines keep theirs.
UI_pzopt_tip_occludedOutlineOpacityPct: How opaque the contour is in daylight; dimmer in the dark and while the zombie fades in or out of sight.
UI_pzopt_tip_mirrors: Wall mirrors, mirrored medicine cabinets and dressers, and window panes reflect what stands in front of them: the floor and the room, the street, and you, the zombies and the cars as their real other side (the game's own models drawn once more through the mirror's plane, lit as they are lit), so a mirror shows your face, not your back. From the game's high camera a wall mirror shows the floor and whoever stands within a couple of squares of it; a window upstairs shows the street below. Someone inside a room seen through a window keeps the reflection over them, as glass does; a closed curtain stops it. The room part of each pane's reflection is worked out once and kept while nothing changes; panes hidden under a roof or behind a building are skipped. Applies on the next launch (mirror tiles are drawn on their own instead of into the chunk pictures).
UI_pzopt_tip_mirrorsWindows: On: window panes reflect as well (subtly, as glass does). Off: no window reflects (wall mirrors and glass props keep theirs). Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_tip_mirrorsWindowPct: How much of a window pane is its reflection. Real glass reflects a few percent head-on, more where the room behind it is dark; higher reads more like a shop window by day. Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_label_mirrorsProps: Mirrors: glass, screens and steel reflect too
UI_pzopt_tip_mirrorsProps: On: the things in a room that are not mirrors or windows reflect as well: glass doors, shop fronts and railings, shower screens, display counters and cases, glass-door fridges, the glass table, switched-off televisions and monitors, the gym's wall mirrors, steel counters, sinks and appliances, toilets. Each surface reflects the way it faces: a glass top shows what stands behind it, a door or a pane what stands in front, faintly as glass does; steel, ceramic and dark screens keep their own look and show the people and cars passing in front as a soft sheen. Their shape comes from the game's own depth maps, so nothing is guessed per object. Reflections fade where you cannot see (out of your sight the prop is dark, so is its reflection). Applies on the next launch (with Mirror and window reflections on).
UI_pzopt_tip_mirrorsPropGlassPct: How much of a glass door, counter or case is its reflection. Real glass reflects a few percent head-on and more at a grazing angle (a glass top more than an upright pane: the game's camera sees tops at 60 degrees). Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_label_mirrorsModels: Mirrors: people and cars in the reflection
UI_pzopt_tip_mirrorsModels: On: characters and vehicles in front of a mirror or window are drawn once more through its plane, so the mirror shows their faces and the side of the car facing it. Off: the reflection is made of what the camera sees (you see their backs). Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_tip_torchSource: A flashlight, lantern, lighter or weapon light shines from the item in your hand, on your webbing or under your gun barrel, at its height, instead of from the middle of your feet: the beam starts at the lens and moves with your arm, a lantern held at your side lights that side, and with Per-pixel lighting the beam, its shadows, the glow in fog and the shadows other people cast from it all start there too. The game's own square-by-square lighting starts from the same spot (never through a wall) and holds still while you stand still. Applies at once.
UI_pzopt_label_torchSourceAim: Light from the torch itself: beam direction
UI_pzopt_tip_torchSourceAim: Where the beam points. Where you look (the game's own) keeps the beam steady on your aim; where the item points makes it follow the flashlight in your hand as you walk and turn, and a flashlight tilted down lights the ground nearer (with Per-pixel lighting).
UI_pzopt_label_torchSourceSelfShadow: Light from the torch itself: your body casts a shadow
UI_pzopt_tip_torchSourceSelfShadow: With Per-pixel lighting: your own body shades the light you carry, so a lantern in one hand leaves the other side of you in a soft shadow, and a light at your hip does not light what is behind you. A torch held out in front is never tested. Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_note_b2d1c4c310: where the item points (follows your hand)
UI_pzopt_tip_godRaysSoftPct: How soft the edges of the shafts and of their sunlit patches are: the light spreads a little the farther it gets from the window, so the shafts blur out instead of ending in hard lines (0: cut exactly by the window frame).
UI_pzopt_tip_godRaysGlintPct: Specks of dust drifting in the shafts now and then catch the sun and glint.
UI_pzopt_label_mirrorsGeometry: Mirrors: the room behind the glass
UI_pzopt_tip_mirrorsGeometry: On: a wall mirror's room is rebuilt behind the glass from the game's own tiles, so the mirror shows what the camera can never see: the far side of the bathtub or the bed in front of it (the furniture's other facing, as the game draws it when you turn it), the floor behind it, and the wall across the room. Off: the reflection is made of what the camera sees, and where that is hidden (behind a table, a bathtub) the floor seen last stands in. Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_label_mirrorsCutawayHoldMs: Mirrors: steady walls by a room corner (ms)
UI_pzopt_tip_mirrorsCutawayHoldMs: The game cuts the walls round you away so you stay in sight; standing or walking by a room's corner it flips a wall between cut and shown every few tenths of a second, and a mirror on that wall blinked in and out with it. A wall with a mirror changes at most once in this time (it still goes at once the first time) and comes back only after it has not been needed for twice this, the game's own cutaway lock that its newer renderer skips. 0: the game's flipping. Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_label_mirrorsViewLateralPct: Mirrors: where you appear along the glass (%)
UI_pzopt_tip_mirrorsViewLateralPct: 0: you appear straight in front of where you stand, as you see yourself in a mirror. 100: the game camera's true reflection, which puts someone a square out from the mirror a square to its side (off a small medicine cabinet). Windows always use the true reflection. Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_tip_mirrorsViewDropPct: How much higher someone farther from the mirror appears in it, as a share of the game camera's true reflection (100: a third of a floor per square out, a head at the sink above the medicine cabinet). 0: at their own height, eye level, below the game's high-hung cabinets. 50: your head in the cabinet from the sink, as if looking slightly down into the mirror. Applies on the next launch.
UI_pzopt_layout_42709e0997: Smoother frames and faster loads. Nothing here changes how the game looks.
UI_pzopt_layout_66e63a052c: Even frame delivery, variable refresh and input latency.
UI_pzopt_layout_c5d5030c62: The car's stutter and rubber banding, and the world arriving at speed.
UI_pzopt_layout_b6e1486958: What the chunk pictures hold and how many are drawn in a frame.
UI_pzopt_layout_6d553419c0: Light refreshes, see-through walls and roofs, fog, rain and puddles.
UI_pzopt_layout_71fb35bc89: The zombie simulation spread over every core, and cheaper checks.
UI_pzopt_layout_30ab777fb5: From launch to the menu, and from Continue to the world.
UI_pzopt_layout_b6ae3f6de1: Windows that answer in the frame you click.
UI_pzopt_layout_e1d976958f: Cores and power, the audio mix, other mods, updates.
UI_pzopt_layout_3472cc224d: Graphics the stock game does not have. Off by default; each card says what it costs.
UI_pzopt_layout_a107f0fd59: Upscalers, dynamic resolution, sprite filtering and HDR output.
UI_pzopt_layout_0518e59abf: Per-pixel light, the real sky's shadows, ambient occlusion and god rays.
UI_pzopt_layout_a4b972eb8c: Water and puddles (reflections, ripples), mirrors and windows, car glass, wet blood.
UI_pzopt_layout_53783e672f: Darkness and colour grading, foliage sway, relief, zombie outlines.
UI_pzopt_layout_61158d5227: The performance overlay (F9), its game-thread profiler and the console log.
UI_pzopt_layout_8d516b6576: Frame times, utilization and what the game thread does, on screen.
UI_pzopt_layout_4c0a5608c6: Chunks arrive faster than their pictures bake, and the car is drawn at its physics steps.
UI_pzopt_layout_4c7403f155: At 120 km/h about 50 new chunks a second reach the screen. Stock bakes each chunk's picture in the frame it arrives, and it draws the car and the camera at the last 100 Hz physics step, so the car rubber-bands against the street. These spread the bakes over frames, draw the car between its physics steps and keep trees in the bake. Rosewood town drive at the 240 cap: stock 153 fps (p99 36 ms), with these 235 fps (p99 8 ms).
UI_pzopt_layout_052198d44c: Low fps in a big horde
UI_pzopt_layout_1387f37c70: Stock runs the whole zombie simulation on the game thread.
UI_pzopt_layout_535b0669c9: Every zombie's animation, decisions and drawing preparation run one after the other on the game thread, while the other cores idle. These run them on every core and skip checks that cannot change anything. The Louisville horde (about 2,000 zombies), same build with these off and on: 46 to 58 fps.
UI_pzopt_layout_2810eac84a: Boot work runs one file at a time, and the loading screen waits for everything.
UI_pzopt_layout_ddbd13fc6c: Stock parses scripts, animations and textures on one thread at boot and shows a loading screen until the whole cell is ready. These do the boot work on several threads with caches, and enter the world from the centre outwards with the last view on screen meanwhile. Launch to menu 7.4 to 5.0 s, Continue to the world 6.5 to 4.0 s.
UI_pzopt_layout_d111ba4f5e: Storms, fog and rain are slow
UI_pzopt_layout_74aa219f4f: Stock redraws fog rows and every wet square each frame.
UI_pzopt_layout_943b28f2e1: Heavy fog is drawn as about 190 screen-wide rows per level, and rain re-packs every particle and puddle every frame. These draw fog in one pass, rain as repeated tiles and keep the puddles on the GPU. 120 km/h drive in heavy fog: 220 to 389 fps; thunderstorm: 83 to 131 fps.
UI_pzopt_layout_0c6fb5ba8f: Input is read early and finished frames queue up for the GPU.
UI_pzopt_layout_3230d6ea9b: Stock reads the keyboard and mouse well before the frame they move is shown, and lets the driver queue frames. These read the newest input when a frame starts, keep the queue short and draw the cursor at the newest mouse position.
UI_pzopt_layout_34e4f8e27f: Borderless never gets variable refresh, and frames reach the screen unevenly.
UI_pzopt_layout_19245da951: A borderless window does not count as fullscreen for the desktop, so G-SYNC / FreeSync stay off, and frames reach the screen as soon as they are ready. These make the window count as fullscreen, keep the frame rate inside the display's range and hand frames over at even steps (judder 3.1 to 0.95 ms).
UI_pzopt_layout_147180e703: Every window redraws every frame, with or without a change.
UI_pzopt_layout_211358f3fc: An open inventory took the Lua UI from 2 to 12 %% of the game thread in stock. These redraw only what changed, the moment you act, and keep the map's labels while the view stays.
UI_pzopt_layout_5cb46b3851: The game's threads land on slow cores and the GPU clock goes up and down.
UI_pzopt_layout_4af7d2732b: On hybrid CPUs the game thread can end up on an efficient core; small GPUs spend frames at full resolution. These place the threads, hold the GPU clock steady, and render the world smaller when the GPU is the limit. The Low-end presets on the home page set them for you (4-core laptop, 120 km/h drive: 44 to 68 fps).
UI_pzopt_layout_0f5123bd68: A mod that patches the same game code can clash with an optimization.
UI_pzopt_layout_8d4e1fc447: PZ Optimization scans the Java mods of each launch and can switch off what they patch. Max performance keeps everything on and reports clashes; Max compatibility switches the affected settings off. The main menu's compatibility check lists what it found.
