UI_pzopt_v8_why_entityShadows_cores: The frame's shadow bricks and casters are gathered on a worker while the world draws: 63-85 us of it in a Louisville horde, 2.4 us left on the game thread.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_entityShadows_gpu: The character and car shaders look up the shade where each part stands: about 27 us of GPU for 40 zombies and 3 cars across a shadow's edge on the desktop, ~0 on a drive.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_entityShadowCasters_gpu: The nearest capsules that can reach each body are tested in its shader: about 0.02 ms a frame on an RTX 4090 in a dense crowd at a shadow's edge, little with few characters.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_entityShadowAoPct_render: A second uniform array per character draw: about 8 us a frame of render thread for 40 zombies standing close together (about 0.01 ms of frame time).
UI_pzopt_v8_why_entityShadowAoPct_cores: The worker that gathers the shadows also picks up to 3 neighbours' capsules for each character: ~22 us of its time in that crowd.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_sunShadowStaticLights_gp: One more shadow area per lit character, at most two lights each: the same cost as a torch's shadow for each.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_sunShadowStaticLights_cp: A line test from each light to the squares the characters stand on, kept for about a second: at most 48 a frame.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_sunShadowRoomLights_gpu: One more shadow area per character in a lit room, the same as a lamp's: at most two lights each.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_sunShadowRoomLights_cpu: The lit rooms near the camera are listed every frame, and a line test from the light to each character in the room, kept for about a second.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_cloudShadows_gpu: World pixels under a cloud read the drifting cloud field and the picture's kept sun share (a clear sky reads nothing): within the noise of the 5K composite alone, ~0.07 ms in the full set on the desktop's town drive.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_reflections_render: The render thread issues the patched chunk and water programs and the characters' mirror pass: its load went 38 to 67 % on the desktop's town drive.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_reflections_gpu: Every chunk picture writes itself where its mirror image lands as it is drawn, and the water reads one value: nothing with no water on screen, +11-15 us at a river, +27-30 us in rain with puddles at 5K.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_reflections_vram: Two 32-bit images at the world picture's size hold the mirrored pixels (alternating frames), plus a small tile map.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_ripples_cores: The rings are sorted into screen tiles on a worker thread each frame (~8 us for ~190 rings), not on the game thread.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_ripples_gpu: The puddle shader reads only the rings sorted into its part of the screen: about 9 us a frame at 5K with 40 walkers in puddles everywhere (19 us on a laptop's iGPU), nothing when it is dry.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_ripplesRain_gpu: The default flipbook is two texture reads a pixel instead of the stock rings' maths: the 5K puddle pass 19-33 us cheaper than stock on an RTX 4090 (cells costs ~0.2 ms more than stock).
UI_pzopt_v8_why_ripplesWake_gpu: The tyre trail is stamped into a world map by a small compute pass the puddles read: about 13 us of GPU at 5K while a car drives through water, nothing otherwise.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_carGlass_render: Each car's glass is one more draw with its own settings: about 3 us of render thread a car (~0.1 ms for a ring of 33 cars).
UI_pzopt_v8_why_carGlass_gpu: A small reflection probe per car is marched through the scene before the cars, then a separate glass program redraws only the window triangles: +10 us with a few cars in view, +54 us for 33 parked cars; nothing with no car on screen.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_carOccupant_render: Each redraw of an occupant's picture is a model draw on the render thread (~30 us warm, 150-200 us cold); drawn only when they move, that is about 3 us a frame parked.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_occludedZombieOutlines_r: Zombies with something in front of them are drawn once more into the mark: +0.02-0.06 ms a frame in a crowd of 60, +0.08 ms in a 300-zombie horde.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_occludedZombieOutlines_g: The zombies' own draws mark what they cover, then one pass draws the contour where they are hidden: ~12 us at 5K, skipped on frames where no zombie can be hidden.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_mirrors_render: The render thread issues each pane's march into its atlas tile (9-17 us a call, at most every 4th frame), one composite a frame (4-8 us) and the mirrored models' flush (~20 us plus ~3 us a model).
UI_pzopt_v8_why_mirrors_gpu: Panes are marched when new or every 30 frames and composited once a frame: +13..34 us a frame with ~30 windows on screen on the desktop at 5K (about 1 % of a 240 fps frame), nothing without one on screen.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_mirrors_vram: The panes' atlases (2048 x 2048 reflection colour, depth and glass masks) stay allocated while the game runs.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_mirrorsWindows_gpu: In a street the windows are most of the panes: each adds its tile to the march and its pixels to the composite (29 windows on screen: +13..34 us a frame on the desktop at 5K).
UI_pzopt_v8_why_mirrorsWallMirrors_gpu: Each wall mirror on screen is drawn every frame instead of in the chunk picture, marched into its tile with its rebuilt room and composited with the other panes; off they bake as in the game.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_mirrorsProps_gpu: Props join the mirrors' composite and model passes, their reflection worked out once a prop and kept: +107..129 us a frame in prop-dense rooms and shops on a laptop (Radeon 890M, 1080p), 0.7 % of a 60 fps frame.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_mirrorsGeometry_vram: The rebuilt rooms are drawn into their own geometry atlas (colour and depth, ~32 MB), only for a pane due for its march, and kept while the room stands.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_mirrorsModels_render: Every mirrored character or car is submitted again through the mirror's plane: a flush of ~20 us plus ~3 us a model on the frames the layer is redrawn (at most 120 a second).
UI_pzopt_v8_why_mirrorsModels_gpu: The models are drawn a second time into the reflection layer, only those at panes you can see: with 24 zombies at a shop front ~11 us a frame on the desktop at 5K.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_bloodWet_cpu: The game thread collects the wet splats on screen, rebuilt only when chunks, visible squares or the camera's chunk change, or every 100 ms: +0.6 % of its time in a fight, 2.3 % with every chunk on screen wet.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_bloodWet_gpu: The wet film is drawn over the floor once a frame, like the puddles: 8.5-9 us in a realistic fight (up to 285 splats), 12-13 us with 4,096 wet splats on screen, on the desktop at 5K.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_bloodWetMinutes_gpu: Longer keeps more splats wet at once, so more films are drawn each frame; shorter dries them sooner (from ~9 us in a fight to ~13 us with every chunk on screen wet, desktop at 5K).
UI_pzopt_v8_why_godRays_cpu: The game thread records the walls, windows, doorways, roofs and crowns of each chunk (11 us a chunk, at most 400 us a frame while chunks arrive), then 2-6 us a frame for the window prisms and the lights.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_godRays_gpu: A visibility volume is traced towards the sun, the sunlit windows draw their light volumes and the haze is tapped inside the chunk composite: 10-14 us a frame on the desktop at 5K, ~7 us on a clear noon.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_godRays_vram: The occupancy grid (256 x 256 squares x 16 levels round the camera) and the visibility and haze volumes at the screen's size.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_godRaysLocal_gpu: Up to 8 nearby lights each draw one screen-blended quad over their reach with the closed-form glow; only at night, in rooms or in fog and rain: ~10 us a frame for all god rays at night on the desktop at 5K.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_godRaysCharShadows_gpu: People near a lit window or doorway become two capsules each that the light volume tests: +2 us with you in a doorway's shaft, +4 us with 6 people at windows, on the desktop at 5K.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_godRaysSpill_gpu: Each lit room's ceiling light by an open door or window draws its glow clipped to the opening, only in fog or rain: the night light pass 21.5 to 27.6 us on the desktop at 5K.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_godRaysBouncePct_gpu: Each sunlit patch adds one box that lights the surfaces round it as a disk light: +17 us a frame at the 60 fps capture cap.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_foliageSway_gpu: The chunk composite moves each plant pixel by the wind as it draws: +19..21 us a frame on the desktop at 5K (1.7 % uncapped), where the game's own wind option costs +348 us.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_foliageSway_vram: Each chunk picture keeps a plant attribute texture: 104 MB at zoom 1, 272 MB zoomed out; those not drawn for 3 s are freed while streaming (142-180 MB).
UI_pzopt_v8_why_foliageSwayTaps_gpu: Each step upwind is one more lookup per plant pixel in the composite: taps 1 (the default) +13..17 us, taps 3 +46 us at 5K on the desktop.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_glints_gpu: Only the flakes that catch a light are drawn, as tiny points: ~0.005 ms a frame on a frosty morning on the desktop at 5K, ~0.012 ms with every outdoor square frosty in full sun, nothing at all without frost, snow or a wet road in a light.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_glintPass_gpu: Measured on the desktop at 5K with every outdoor square frosty in full sun: particles ~0.012 ms of GPU a frame, compact ~0.019 ms, diamonds ~0.10 ms. Nothing at all without frost, snow or a wet road in a light.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_glintAsync_cpu: Wet town road at night with two cars' lights and the street lamps, zoom 2.5, on the desktop: ~0.004 ms of the game thread a frame on, ~0.06-0.07 ms off.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_glintAsync_cores: The work moves to a thread of its own: ~0.06 ms a frame there in the same scene, nothing without frost, snow or a wet road in a light.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_groundCoverWind_gpu: At most 32 small leaves in one draw: ~0.007 ms of GPU a frame on the desktop while they fly, nothing otherwise.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_groundTracks_cpu: Stamping a car and a few hundred walkers into the ground map: a few microseconds a frame on the game thread.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_groundTracks_gpu: The wheels and feet are pressed into the ground map on the graphics card (a microsecond or two a frame while something moves), the tracks are drawn into the ground when its chunk is redrawn, about 5 us a time; with Tracks: show at once the fresh ones also each frame until then.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_groundTracks_vram: The ground map round the player: 16 MB.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_groundTracksRealtime_gpu: Only the squares stamped since their chunk's last redraw are drawn again each frame: about 2 us a frame with a few people on a lawn, 15-25 us under a horde of 200 on bare earth, nothing on roads and once the chunks are redrawn.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_groundTracksPersist_disk: A small file per 16 x 16 chunks you left tracks in, written in the background every 30 seconds and when you move on.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_grassBlades_gpu: Tens of thousands of blades near the player: about 50 to 150 us a frame at 5K on the desktop, only while grass is in reach.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_grassBlades_vram: The blades' buffers and the wind and trample maps: a few MB.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_grassBladeRadius_gpu: The blade count grows with the square of the reach.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_grassBladeDensityPct_gpu: The blade pass costs in proportion to the blades drawn.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_darknessFloorPct_cpu: The floor is applied as the game thread reads each square's light: 17-26 us a frame on a streaming route. Changing it re-reads every loaded square and re-bakes the chunk pictures on screen once.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_colorGrading_cores: The colour table is baked on a low-priority worker (about 24 ms) only when the hour or the weather moves the look, then uploaded in ~30 us.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_colorGrading_gpu: One table lookup per pixel replaces the stock screen shader's colour maths and its 3D-noise grain: the screen pass costs 72 instead of 100 us at 5K on the desktop.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_pixelLight_cpu: A light change only marks a small light grid dirty instead of re-baking chunk pictures, so moving torches, headlights and lightning stop causing re-bakes; packing the grid takes 9-29 us a frame.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_pixelLight_gpu: The chunk composite multiplies each pixel by the interpolated light and draws torch and headlight cones per pixel: +50..190 us a frame over the stock program on a laptop (Radeon 890M, 1080p).
UI_pzopt_v8_why_pixelLight_vram: The per-square light grid round the camera lives on the GPU as texture arrays, about 12 MB.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_pplPointLights_gpu: Every chunk picture a lamp or fire reaches needs the lit program instead of the light-free one; off, only pictures near torches and headlights pay for per-pixel light.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_voxelLight_gpu: Compute traces the lamps and floods the sky only where something changed and relights those chunk layers: a still scene costs about what per-pixel lighting alone does, a 120 km/h night drive +31 us a frame (1.7 %) at 5K.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_voxelLight_vram: A ~60 MB light volume round the camera plus a 144 MB cache of per-chunk light layers.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_voxelLightSkyMethod_gpu: Worked out again when buildings change: flood ~32 us of compute for the whole window, cascades ~0.9 ms and cones ~2 ms (17 rays a cell) on the desktop at 5K.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_pplShadows_gpu: The shadow map is built on the GPU only when the torch or the world round it changes (~0.2 ms at 5K on the desktop, zoomed in), kept while you stand; reading it adds ~0.05 ms (sharp edges) to ~0.1 ms (soft) a frame where the beam falls.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_pplShadows_vram: A 2048 x 2048 depth map (16 MB) and an 8 MB list of the cells it draws.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_pplShadowFilter_gpu: Soft reads the shadow map 8 times a pixel instead of once where the beam falls: about +0.07 ms a frame on the desktop at 5K, zoomed in.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_relief_gpu: Each chunk picture is encoded once after it bakes (~27 us a bake) and the sun and moon relit four pictures at a time when they move a step (~100 us); a 120 km/h drive adds ~67 us a frame to the bakes.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_relief_vram: Two bytes for every texel of every chunk picture (the relief code and the baked light factor, ~2 MB a 1024 x 1024 picture), up to a 512 MB budget while streaming.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_reliefTorchShadowSteps_g: Each torch-lit pixel follows the light a few texels across the relief: +124 us a frame in the composite with 4 steps, on the desktop at 5K.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlaySampling_render: Each presented frame gets a timestamp and a ring entry, and its draw commands are bracketed by a GL timer query (not on a Mac, where Apple's timer queries are slow).
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlaySampling_cores: A low-priority thread wakes twice a second for the game and render threads' CPU time and the GPU busy share; the slow Windows load counters are read only while the overlay is shown or logging.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlay_cpu: While shown the game thread recomputes the statistics and lays out the panel every 250 ms, queues the frame-graph bars every frame, and pauses briefly for each stack sample the tree and verdict take.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlay_render: The render thread draws the panel texture (redrawn at each refresh) and the live frame bars every frame, on top of the sampling's timer queries.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlay_cores: Showing it starts the background samplers: CPU / GPU load and power twice a second, and the game thread's stack 25 times a second for the tree and the verdict.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlayLog_cpu: The log keeps the game-thread stack sampler running even with the overlay hidden: each sample pauses the game thread briefly (25 a second by default).
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlayLog_render: The render thread formats and writes each frame's row a few frames late, once that frame's GPU timer has resolved.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlayLog_cores: The background threads keep sampling the load, the power counters and the stacks for the files while the overlay is hidden.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlayLog_disk: One CSV row a frame to Zomboid/pzopt-overlay.out through a 64 KB buffer, plus pzopt-gamethread.out each second and pzopt-power.out twice a second.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlayTree_cpu: The tree needs the game thread's stack sampled (25 a second by default): each sample stops it at its next safepoint for a stack walk of tens of microseconds.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlayTree_cores: The sampler thread walks each stack and folds it into phases, sub-phases and hot methods (~80 us a sample).
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlayGraph_cpu: With the graph's redraw rate at 0 (the default) the game thread queues one sprite per bar every frame, plus the GPU time bars: about 480 for the last 240 frames.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlayGraph_render: The render thread draws those bar sprites every frame.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlayGraphHz_cpu: 15 to 60 redraws a second into the panel texture replace the ~480 bar sprites the game thread queues every frame at 0 (the default); a lower rate is cheaper and the bars move in steps.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlayGraphHz_render: The render thread draws one textured quad a frame and repaints the graph's rectangle only at this rate, instead of every bar every frame.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlayFlame_cpu: It needs the game thread's stack samples (each a brief pause); with \"Draw the overlay as one texture\" off every box and label is a sprite every frame, the overlay's heaviest element.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlayFlame_cores: The sampler thread keeps the last 5 s of folded stacks for the graph.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_gameThreadProfileHz_cpu: Each sample stops the game thread at its next safepoint for a stack walk: about 0.15 ms a sample on a MacBook, so 100 a second takes ~1.5 % of its time and 25 about a quarter of that.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_gameThreadProfileHz_core: The sampler thread walks and folds each stack (~80 us a sample), so its load grows with the rate.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlayTexture_cpu: The game thread queues one quad a frame instead of thousands of glyph and box sprites: drawn as sprites they cost 12 % of the frame rate on a game-thread-bound laptop.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlayTexture_render: The render thread draws one textured quad instead of thousands of sprites and repaints the texture only at each refresh.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlayTexture_gpu: One quad instead of thousands of small blended sprites every frame.
UI_pzopt_v8_why_overlayRefreshMs_cpu: Each refresh sorts the window's frame times, merges the stack tree and lays out the panel on the game thread: a longer interval does it less often (250 ms: four times a second), at the price of slower numbers.
